turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about his zero from his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I entered the zero before I called you. That was wrong, and I own it.
Okay. Now the basis, Hale. What do you have?

Here's the version history. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58 PM another 794. Then small edits. No earlier drafts.
And before that zero went in, did anyone sit Owen down and ask him about it, the way 4.1 says you must?
So he wrote nothing until almost midnight the night before it was due, and then fourteen hundred words appeared in six minutes.
You still haven't told me who decided on that zero, Hale.
What was he doing at midnight that night?
I'm not the one being questioned here, Hale, and his home is not on the table. Who decided?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology and the name of the person who decided on it, and that nothing be placed on Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to be told who decided on it; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never put on the table before the meeting ended.
What moved her: Owning in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her earned a small sign of ground, because it took away the procedural grievance she walked in with.
What cost ground: Asking what Owen was doing at midnight turned her into a witness about her own home, which she will never accept, and it pushed her back onto procedure.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the work on the night of Wednesday, October 28, between 11:31 and 11:58 PM, the night before it was due, and your midnight question came very close to that night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after showing the version history, answer her question about whether Owen was spoken to and who decided, then offer the private supervised reassessment under procedure 4.4 instead of asking about that night.
